summary: Use two indices moving through a sequence (toward each other, or both forward at different speeds) to avoid nested loops when the data is sorted or has a structural property to exploit.
recognize_when: The input array or linked list is sorted (or can be sorted without losing needed info)
You need to find a pair/triplet satisfying a sum or comparison condition
You're comparing elements from both ends of a sequence (palindrome checks, container/area problems)
A brute force pairwise check would be O(n^2) but the sorted order lets you eliminate possibilities monotonically
Detecting cycles or finding midpoints in a linked list (fast/slow pointer variant)

complexity.notes: Each pointer traverses the sequence at most once (or O(n log n) total if an initial sort is required); no extra data structures needed beyond the pointers themselves.

gotchas: Forgetting to sort first when the pointers rely on monotonic ordering to decide which side to move
Off-by-one on the loop condition (left < right vs left <= right) causing missed or duplicate pairs
Not skipping duplicate values when the problem asks for unique pairs/triplets (e.g. 3Sum)
examples: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
